## Observation

1\. What is recommended on your home page right now? Can you explain why?

- There are music and video commentaries because I usually listen to songs on youtube while doing my work and I would watch commentaries when I'm eating. 

  ![][image1]

2\. Search for something unusual — does the recommendation feed change?

- Yes, there is one video about Champions League recommended in my feed after I search for “Premium League” and engage with one of the videos.

  ![][image2]

3\. Can you observe differences across content types, or identify factors that might cause  
recommendations to differ across users? Distinguish clearly between what you observed and what you are hypothesising.

- Of the 20 videos on my homepage, 15 are music playlists and 5 are vlogs. I think music dominates because I prefer to listen to them on Youtube rather than Spotify.

4\. Can you find any content that seems inappropriate or harmful being recommended?

- No

5\. How transparent is the system about WHY it recommends something?

- Youtube is transparent about why it recommends something, they view our habits and compare with those that are similar and use that information to suggest other content we may want to watch. Youtube does this with the principle of helping people find the videos they want to watch and that will give them value. This is explained in their official blog. 

| System name | Youtube Recommendations Algorithm |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Group members** | Kasih, Nurien, Kesshi, Anis, Alyaa |
| **1\. What problem does this system solve? Who benefits?**  | **Problem**: Homepage is filled with videos that are trending and have the most views but not something a specific user wants to watch. On top of that, the majority of Youtube’s viewership did not come from the homepage, it came from searches and shared links off the platform.  **Beneficiaries**: This benefits the users and also Youtube. With contents tailored to the user’s specific interests, users will continuously discover new videos that align with their interest thus increasing profit for Youtube for usage increment.  |
| **2\. Which AI stack layer is most visible to users?**  | Application Development layer: There are options for what kind of contents to watch at the top of the homepage. The selections are curated from our viewing habits.  |
| **3\. Quality dimensions — at least 3, with measurement method**  | **Quality of personalization Measurement**: Does engagement with a specific video improve tailoring **Transparency and user control Measurement:** Can users change settings like how much data to provide or if the user can pause, edit or delete Youtube search and history. **Diversity Measurement:** Does recommended videos vary in creators, formats, and viewpoints? |
| **4\. What did the system do WELL? Give a specific example.**  | Youtube does well in creating “Mix” playlist for the music I listen to. So, when I'm watching a music video, it will automatically shuffle to the next song on the mix.  |
| **5\. What did it do POORLY? Give a specific example.**  | Youtube may recommend content that is too similar to what users have watched before for example, after searching for “Premier League” and watching a related video, a Champions League video appeared in my recommendations. It keeps recommending similar football content which causes limited exposure to other topics. |
| **6\. Responsible AI risks — at least 2\. Who is harmed and how?**  | Risk 1 – Filter Bubble: Repeatedly recommending similar videos limits users’ exposure to different topics and viewpoints. Risk 2 – Privacy: Using users’ viewing history may raise privacy concerns if they do not understand how data is used. Risk 3 – Harmful Content: Misleading videos may be recommended to cause inaccurate information to users. |
| **7\. If you could fix ONE thing, what and why?**  | Improve content diversity by recommending videos from different topics, helping users discover new interests and viewpoints. |
